title: [Update 2] My Claude-built sea after 13 passes, now playable. You said the loop mattered more than the looks, so here's the beta
author: Panda5Studio
selftext:
Follow-up to [my last update](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/s/rrJqoIeDuY). Same temple, same camera path, but this time the final shot transitions into actual gameplay.

Thanks again for that thread. One comment stuck with me more than the rest because it went straight to the point.

**"Visuals aren't the real question. The loop is."**

Fair point. I said I'd put a playable build on itch.io while Steam reviews my developer account, so here it is:

[https://dept47-games.itch.io/technically-fishing](https://dept47-games.itch.io/technically-fishing)

* Free for Windows / macOS, no account or email needed
* Mostly tested on Apple silicon Macs. On Windows I've only confirmed it launches on an older PC. Intel Macs are untested
* Stage 1 and the entrance to Stage 2
* Loop: dive, spear, surface, sell, upgrade

In the video: swim out, chase a school of parrotfish, spear one, surface, and sell it at the guild. And it's not just the spear — later in the demo you can get a water gun that fires charged shots straight through several fish.

**How it's built now**

* A bot does the first pass as a tester to save time. Claude wrote an autoplay script that takes jobs from the guild, dives, sells, and clears the whole demo. It runs through each new build before I do, so I can focus my own playtesting on how the game feels. When I hit a job I couldn't finish in my own run, the bot replayed it to track down why.
* I couldn't get the first launch fast enough, so I added an opening cutscene. The first start has to do a lot of prep before the title screen shows up and I couldn't get that time down, so now an intro plays while the game gets ready in the background.

**What I'm still tuning**

How sensitive the fish should be. Too relaxed and it stops feeling like the sea; too skittish and it loses that easy pick-up-and-play feel. Push it far enough and the difficulty spikes until it becomes a different game. Still figuring out where it should sit between game and realism, and how hard it should be.

Last time I learned the final call has to be human. Same this time, just with a bot doing the first lap.

comments.author: Sophie_Ward67
comments.body: nice to see u turned feedback into playable demo. dive, catch, sell and upgrade loop sounds like good starting point

replies.author: Panda5Studio
replies.body: Thanks! That loop is the base I want to build on. Right now I'm tuning how the fish react to you, so each dive feels a bit different.

replies.author: SubZeroSunExodus
replies.body:
That sounds very interesting. Thanks for sharing. 

Also just curious how much tokens (for first pass and by the 13th pass) or which plan did you do this on?

replies.author: Panda5Studio
replies.body:
Good question! I run a few projects in parallel so it's hard to be exact, but up to the 13th rework of the ocean/sea system, ccusage showed roughly $2,500 in API-equivalent usage for everything combined.  
I'm on the $200/month Max plan though, so that's all I actually pay. There are hourly + weekly limits that reset, so I plan heavy /loop sessions around them.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: I love to see the progress :)

replies.author: Panda5Studio
replies.body: Thanks! Your schools-of-fish suggestion last time is part of why there's a parrotfish school to chase in this clip.

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: I mean you can definitely see the progress no doubt about it, when you get to the point that is "before" you think "omg this is so good" but once you get to a point where it is now you think "damn it was not that good after all" :D

replies.author: Panda5Studio
replies.body: Ha, that’s so true. Every version felt like the best one at the time. Your feedback and everyone else’s comments are a big part of how it got here, so thanks for following along since the first post.

replies.body: Thank you! I only vaguely remember Aquanaut's Holiday, but I know Artdink from the A-Train games. Being compared to one of their games is a big compliment.
